question: The gravitational force between the Earth and a body of mass ‘m’ kg is ‘F’ N. What will be the gravitational force between the body and the Earth if the mass of the body is increased to ‘4m’ kg? (Keep all the other parameters the same)
solution:
The correct answer is __**4F N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation**, every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force that is **directly proportional** to the product of their **masses** and **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** between their centers.
 
• The mathematical expression for this force is **F = G (M × m) / r²**, where **G** is the **Gravitational Constant**, **M** is the mass of the **Earth**, **m** is the mass of the **body**, and **r** is the distance between them.
 
• In the initial scenario, the force is given as **F**. If the mass of the body **m** is increased to **4m** while keeping the mass of the Earth **M** and the distance **r** constant, the new force **F'** is calculated as: **F' = G (M × 4m) / r²**.
 
• By rearranging the equation, we get **F' = 4 × [G (M × m) / r²]**. Since the term in the bracket is the original force **F**, the new force becomes **4F**. ***Hence, the gravitational force increases by four times.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):** It is a scalar quantity and its value is **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**. This value was first experimentally determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** and remains constant everywhere in the universe.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight:** While **mass** is the amount of matter in a body and remains constant (**m**), **weight** is the **gravitational force** exerted by the Earth on that body (**W = mg**). If the mass of an object increases, its weight increases proportionally.
 
• **Inverse Square Law:** The gravitational force is highly sensitive to **distance**. If the distance between the Earth and the body were **doubled**, the force would decrease to **one-fourth (F/4)** of its original value.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** On the surface of the Earth, the value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It is derived from the formula **g = GM / r²**, showing that the acceleration of a falling object does not depend on the **mass of the object** itself, but the force acting on it does.
 
• **Earth's Characteristics:** The **Earth** has a mass of approximately **5.97 × 10²⁴ kg** and a mean radius of about **6,371 km**. These parameters define the strength of the **gravitational field** we experience daily.
